message.content: {"back_translation":"It was on a gloomy night of November that I saw the accomplishment of my labors. With an anxiety that bordered on agony, I gathered around me the instruments of life, in order to breathe a spark of existence into the inanimate thing that lay at my feet. It was already one o'clock in the morning; the rain drummed mournfully against the windowpanes, and my candle was almost consumed, when, by the half-extinguished glow, I saw the dull and yellowish eye of the creature open; it breathed with difficulty, and a convulsive movement shook its limbs.\n\nHow to describe my emotions before this catastrophe, or how to depict the wretch whom with such infinite pains and cares I had striven to form? His limbs were well proportioned, and I had chosen his features for their beauty. Beauty! — Great God! His yellow skin barely covered the work of the muscles and arteries lying beneath; his hair was of a glossy black, wavy; his teeth of a pearl-like whiteness; but these riches only formed a more horrible contrast with his watery eyes, which seemed almost the same color as the greyish-white sockets in which they were set, his withered complexion and his black, straight lips.","changes":[{"shelley":"dull yellow eye","translation":"l'œil terne et jaunâtre","back_translation":"the dull and yellowish eye","category":"softening","rationale":"\"Jaunâtre\" (yellowish) weakens the flat, stark \"yellow\" and splits the compact phrase into two adjectives."},{"shelley":"it breathed hard","translation":"elle respira péniblement","back_translation":"it breathed with difficulty","category":"shift in meaning","rationale":"\"Hard\" suggests forceful, heavy breathing, while \"péniblement\" suggests laboured, painful breathing, a slightly different image."},{"shelley":"the rain pattered dismally","translation":"la pluie tambourinait lugubrement","back_translation":"the rain drummed mournfully","category":"intensification","rationale":"\"Tambouriner\" (to drum) is louder and heavier than \"pattered\", and \"lugubrement\" is more funereal than \"dismally\"."},{"shelley":"Beautiful!—Great God!","translation":"De la beauté ! — Grand Dieu !","back_translation":"Beauty! — Great God!","category":"shift in meaning","rationale":"The ironic echo of the adjective \"beautiful\" becomes the noun \"beauty\", which slightly alters the bitter repetition of his own word."},{"shelley":"his hair was of a lustrous black, and flowing","translation":"sa chevelure était d'un noir lustré, ondoyante","back_translation":"his hair was of a glossy black, wavy","category":"shift in meaning","rationale":"\"Ondoyante\" (undulating, wavy) is not quite \"flowing\", and \"chevelure\" is a more poetic word for hair."},{"shelley":"these luxuriances","translation":"ces richesses","back_translation":"these riches","category":"shift in meaning","rationale":"\"Luxuriances\" implies lush abundance, while \"richesses\" suggests valuable assets, losing the sense of excessive growth."},{"shelley":"the dun white sockets","translation":"les orbites d'un blanc grisâtre","back_translation":"the sockets of a greyish white","category":"shift in meaning","rationale":"\"Dun\" means dull brownish-grey; \"grisâtre\" drops the brown tint and is slightly vaguer."},{"shelley":"shrivelled complexion","translation":"son teint flétri","back_translation":"his withered complexion","category":"softening","rationale":"\"Flétri\" (withered, faded) is a little more conventional and less harshly physical than \"shrivelled\"."},{"shelley":"in which they were set","translation":"où ils étaient enchâssés","back_translation":"in which they were enshrined/mounted","category":"intensification","rationale":"\"Enchâssés\" is a jeweller's term (as of a gem in a setting), a more elevated image than the plain \"set\"."},{"shelley":"I had selected his features as beautiful","translation":"j'avais choisi ses traits pour leur beauté","back_translation":"I had chosen his features for their beauty","category":"shift in meaning","rationale":"The French states the reason for the choice (their beauty) rather than the creator's judgment (\"as beautiful\"), removing some of the subjective irony."}],"note":"The French is close and complete, with no real omissions and a consistently elevated literary register (\"labeurs\", \"enchâssés\", \"nacre\", \"chevelure\"). Its small shifts tend toward polish and slightly more formal diction, though a few words are heightened (\"tambourinait\"). The loss of Frankenstein's ironic echo \"Beautiful!\" is probably the most noteworthy change, though it may be an unavoidable grammatical consequence."}
